```{r}
   select(.draw,Cal_Yr, .prediction, pred_paid,Acc_Yr, Dev_Yr,model_id) 
 
 
 model_3_pred_intermediate <-  left_join(model_3_pred, 
                                         future_inflation_forecast,
                                         by = join_by(.draw, Cal_Yr)) |>
   mutate(pred_paid_infl = pred_paid * Accum_Infl_Index_Mid_Adj) 
 
 
 
 model_3_pred_name <-left_join( model_3_pred_intermediate, 
                                title_df, by = join_by( model_id))
 
 model_3_pred_tot_rsv <- model_3_pred_name |>
   ungroup() |>
   select(.draw, pred_paid_infl,model_name) |>
   group_by( .draw,model_name) |>
   summarise(tot_rsv = sum(pred_paid_infl),
             tot_rsv_m = sum(pred_paid_infl/1000000),
             .groups = "keep")
 
 
 
 p5 <-  ggplot(model_3_pred_tot_rsv , aes(x=tot_rsv_m, color =model_name)) +
   stat_ecdf(geom = "step")+
   labs(title="Total Reserve Estimate\n Simulated Future Inflation",
        x="Total Reserve Estimate in Millions",
        y="Cumulative Distribution",
        caption = caption_label)+

 model_3_pred_Acc_Yr_rsv <- model_3_pred_name |>
   ungroup() |>
   select(.draw, pred_paid_infl,model_name, Acc_Yr) |>
   group_by( .draw,model_name, Acc_Yr) |>

             .groups = "keep")
 
 p6 <- model_3_pred_Acc_Yr_rsv %>%

 model_acc_yr_rsv <- rbind(model_1_pred_Acc_Yr_rsv,
                           model_2_pred_Acc_Yr_rsv,
                           model_3_pred_Acc_Yr_rsv)
 
 model_tot_rsv <- rbind(model_1_pred_tot_rsv,
                        model_2_pred_tot_rsv,
                        model_3_pred_tot_rsv)
 
 
 p7 <-  ggplot( model_tot_rsv , aes(x=tot_rsv_m, color =model_name)) +

 p8 <- model_acc_yr_rsv %>%

   labs(title = "Accident Year Ultimate Reserve Estimates\n Simulated Future Inflation ",

        caption = caption_label)+

 return(list(p1, p2, p3, p4, p5, p6, p7, p8) )
 
  
}





```


# Read in the Excel files containing the raw data and the inflation indexes. 
# then make a series of data transformations and save three types of files;
#  the data set used for training, the data set used for the forecast and
# the data set that is summarized to build the method of moment estimates for
# either the random group data set or the non-random group data set

```{r}


# Create the input raw data table from Excel file

# The "_9_" in the data set title is simply a note to myself to identify
# the data sets used in the inflation examples as the 9th pass at building
# a data set.

Case_Inflation_Raw_Data <- read_excel("Case_Inflation_9_train.xlsx")

# include the data set with groups created by assigning a random number 
# between 1 and 10 to each claim then summarizing the individual claims

Case_Inflation_ran_grp_Raw_Data <- read_excel("Case_Inflation_ran_grp_9_train.xlsx")

Case_Inflation_Infl_Index <-read_excel("Cal_Yr_Infl_Case_Inflation.xlsx")

# Create the skeleton explanatory development year data set 

Case_Inflation_Dates <- Case_Inflation_Raw_Data |>
  summarize( max_Acc_Yr = max(Acc_Yr),
             min_Acc_Yr = min(Acc_Yr),
             max_Dev_Yr = max(Dev_Yr),
             min_Dev_Yr = min(Dev_Yr),
             min_Cal_Yr = min(Cal_Yr))



Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Skeleton <- Case_Inflation_Dates |>
  expand_grid(Acc_Yr= min_Acc_Yr:max_Acc_Yr, 
              Dev_Yr=min_Dev_Yr:max_Dev_Yr) |>
  mutate(
    Ln_Dev_Yr = log(Dev_Yr),
    Inv_Dev_Yr = 1/Dev_Yr,
    Dev_Yr_Sqrd = Dev_Yr ^2,
    Dev_Yr_Cbd = Dev_Yr ^3,
    
  )



# Create the transformed Development Year Variables


Cap_Var_DF <- Case_Inflation_Dates |>
  expand_grid(Dev_Yr=min_Dev_Yr:max_Dev_Yr,
              Cap =min_Dev_Yr:max_Dev_Yr) |>
  select(Dev_Yr,Cap,max_Dev_Yr) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Cap,
    names_prefix = "Cap_Dev_Yr_",
    values_from = Cap  ) |>
  mutate(
    across(starts_with("Cap"), ~if_else(.x <=Dev_Yr, .x,Dev_Yr)) )


Cap_Var_Sqrd_DF <- Case_Inflation_Dates |>
  expand_grid(Dev_Yr=min_Dev_Yr:max_Dev_Yr,
              Cap =min_Dev_Yr:max_Dev_Yr) |>
  select(Dev_Yr,Cap,max_Dev_Yr) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Cap,
    names_prefix = "Cap_Dev_Yr_Sqrd_",
    values_from = Cap  ) |>
  mutate(
    across(starts_with("Cap"), ~if_else(.x <=Dev_Yr, .x,Dev_Yr)),
    across(starts_with("Cap"), ~.x ^2 ))


Cap_Var_Ln_DF <- Case_Inflation_Dates |>
  expand_grid(Dev_Yr=min_Dev_Yr:max_Dev_Yr,
              Cap =min_Dev_Yr:max_Dev_Yr) |>
  select(Dev_Yr,Cap,max_Dev_Yr) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Cap,
    names_prefix = "Cap_Dev_Yr_Ln_",
    values_from = Cap  ) |>
  mutate(
    across(starts_with("Cap"), ~if_else(.x <=Dev_Yr, .x,Dev_Yr)),
    across(starts_with("Cap"), ~log(.x) ))





Spline_Var_DF <- Case_Inflation_Dates |>
  expand_grid(Dev_Yr=min_Dev_Yr:max_Dev_Yr,
              Spline =min_Dev_Yr:max_Dev_Yr) |>
  select(Dev_Yr,Spline,max_Dev_Yr) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Spline,
    names_prefix = "Spline_Dev_Yr_",
    values_from = Spline  )|>
  mutate(
    across(starts_with("Spline"), ~if_else(.x <= Dev_Yr,Dev_Yr - .x, 0 ))
  )


Spline_Var_Sqrd_DF <- Case_Inflation_Dates |>
  expand_grid(Dev_Yr=min_Dev_Yr:max_Dev_Yr,
              Spline =min_Dev_Yr:max_Dev_Yr) |>
  select(Dev_Yr,Spline,max_Dev_Yr) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Spline,
    names_prefix = "Spline_Dev_Yr_Sqrd_",
    values_from = Spline  )|>
  mutate(
    across(starts_with("Spline"), ~if_else(.x <= Dev_Yr,Dev_Yr - .x, 0 )),
    across(starts_with("Spline"), ~.x ^2 ))

Spline_Var_Ln_DF <- Case_Inflation_Dates |>
  expand_grid(Dev_Yr=min_Dev_Yr:max_Dev_Yr,
              Spline =min_Dev_Yr:max_Dev_Yr) |>
  select(Dev_Yr,Spline,max_Dev_Yr) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Spline,
    names_prefix = "Spline_Dev_Yr_Ln_",
    values_from = Spline  )|>
  mutate(
    across(starts_with("Spline"), ~if_else(.x <= Dev_Yr,Dev_Yr - .x, 0 )),
    across(starts_with("Spline"), ~if_else(.x >0 ,log(.x), 0 )))


Factor_Var_DF <- Case_Inflation_Dates |>
  expand_grid(Dev_Yr=min_Dev_Yr:max_Dev_Yr,
              Factor =min_Dev_Yr:max_Dev_Yr) |>
  select(Dev_Yr,Factor,max_Dev_Yr) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Factor,
    names_prefix = "Factor_Dev_Yr_",
    values_from = Factor  ) |>
  mutate(
    across(starts_with("Factor"), ~if_else(.x <=Dev_Yr, .x,Dev_Yr)) ,
    across(starts_with("Factor"), ~as_factor(.x)))

# create data set with report year one reported count

Acc_Yr_Report_Year_1_Rptd_Cnt <- Case_Inflation_Raw_Data |>
          select(Acc_Yr, Rptd_Cnt_Yr_1) |>
          unique()

# Combine the Skeleton and Transformed Variable files for training data set


Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Complete  <- Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Skeleton |>
  left_join(Case_Inflation_Raw_Data, by = join_by(Acc_Yr, Dev_Yr))|>
  left_join(Cap_Var_DF, by = join_by(Dev_Yr)) |>
  left_join(Cap_Var_Sqrd_DF, by = join_by(Dev_Yr) )|>
  left_join(Spline_Var_DF, by = join_by(Dev_Yr) )|>
  left_join(Spline_Var_Sqrd_DF, by = join_by(Dev_Yr)) |>
  left_join(Spline_Var_Ln_DF, by = join_by(Dev_Yr)) |>
  left_join(Cap_Var_Ln_DF, by = join_by(Dev_Yr)) |>
  left_join(Factor_Var_DF, by = join_by(Dev_Yr)) |>
  left_join(Case_Inflation_Infl_Index, by = join_by(Cal_Yr)) |>
  mutate(
        Paid_Incr_Cnt_Freq = Paid_Cnt_Incr/Rptd_Cnt_Yr_1,
         Mean_Payment = if_else(Paid_Cnt_Incr == 0,
                                NA,
                                Incr_Paid / Paid_Cnt_Incr),
         Infl_Index_Pct = Infl_Index -1,
         Ln_Mean_Payment = if_else(Mean_Payment == 0,
                                   NA,log(Mean_Payment)),
         Incr_PP = Incr_Paid/ Rptd_Cnt_Yr_1,
         Ln_Incr_PP = if_else(Incr_PP == 0,
                              NA,
                              log(Incr_PP)),
         Incr_PP_Defl = Incr_PP/ Accum_Infl_Index_Mid,
         Ln_Incr_PP_Defl = if_else( Incr_PP_Defl == 0,
                                    NA,
                                    log(Incr_PP_Defl)),
         Mean_Payment_Defl = Mean_Payment/ Accum_Infl_Index_Mid,
         Ln_Mean_Payment_Defl = if_else(Mean_Payment_Defl == 0,
                                        NA,
                                        log(Mean_Payment_Defl)),
         Cal_Yr_Time = Cal_Yr - min_Cal_Yr +1,
         Z_Count= if_else(Paid_Cnt_Incr ==0,1,0),
        Disp_Rate = round(if_else( Acc_Yr == lag(Acc_Yr) & is.na(lag(Acc_Yr)) == FALSE  ,
                                   (Incr_Clsd_W_Pay_Cnt + Incr_Clsd_W_O_Pay_Cnt) /
                                     (Cum_Rptd_Cnt - lag(Cum_Rptd_Cnt)+ lag(Open_Cnt)),
                                   (Incr_Clsd_W_Pay_Cnt + Incr_Clsd_W_O_Pay_Cnt) /
                                     Cum_Rptd_Cnt),3))

# Data set for random group. Given this data set was only used for the 
# method of moments estimate of either sigma for lognormal or shape for Gamma
# there was no need to include all of the transformed development year variables.


Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_ran_grp  <- left_join(Case_Inflation_ran_grp_Raw_Data ,
                                                  
                                                   Acc_Yr_Report_Year_1_Rptd_Cnt,
                                                   join_by(Acc_Yr)) |>
  rename(Rptd_Cnt_Yr_1_ran_grp= Rptd_Cnt_Yr_1.x,
         Rptd_Cnt_Yr_1 =Rptd_Cnt_Yr_1.y) |>
  left_join(Case_Inflation_Infl_Index, by = join_by(Cal_Yr)) |>
  mutate(max_Dev_Yr = max(Dev_Yr),
         Paid_Incr_Cnt_Freq = Paid_Cnt_Incr/Rptd_Cnt_Yr_1_ran_grp,
         Mean_Payment = if_else( Paid_Cnt_Incr == 0, 
                                 NA,
                                 Incr_Paid / Paid_Cnt_Incr),
         Infl_Index_Pct = Infl_Index -1,
         Ln_Mean_Payment = if_else(is.na(Mean_Payment),
                                   NA ,
                                   log(Mean_Payment))
         ,
         Incr_PP = Incr_Paid/ Rptd_Cnt_Yr_1_ran_grp,
         Ln_Incr_PP = if_else(Incr_PP == 0, 
                              NA ,
                              log(Incr_PP)),
         
         Incr_PP_Defl = Incr_PP/ Accum_Infl_Index_Mid,
         
         Ln_Incr_PP_Defl = if_else( Incr_PP_Defl == 0,
                                    NA ,
                                    log(Incr_PP_Defl)),
         
         Mean_Payment_Defl = if_else(is.na(Mean_Payment),
                                     NA ,
                                     Mean_Payment/ Accum_Infl_Index_Mid),
         Ln_Mean_Payment_Defl = if_else( is.na(Mean_Payment_Defl),
                                         NA ,
                                         log(Mean_Payment_Defl)) ,
         
         Z_Count= if_else(Paid_Cnt_Incr ==0,1,0),
         Disp_Rate = round(if_else( Acc_Yr == lag(Acc_Yr) & is.na(lag(Acc_Yr)) == FALSE  ,
                                    (Incr_Clsd_W_Pay_Cnt + Incr_Clsd_W_O_Pay_Cnt) /
                                      (Cum_Rptd_Cnt - lag(Cum_Rptd_Cnt)+ lag(Open_Cnt)),
                                    (Incr_Clsd_W_Pay_Cnt + Incr_Clsd_W_O_Pay_Cnt) /
                                      Cum_Rptd_Cnt),3)) |>
  arrange(Dev_Yr,Acc_Yr,ran_grp)



#combine files for future data set

Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Future  <- Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Skeleton |>
  left_join(Case_Inflation_Raw_Data, by = join_by(Acc_Yr, Dev_Yr))|>
  
  left_join(Acc_Yr_Report_Year_1_Rptd_Cnt, by = join_by(Acc_Yr))|>
  rename(Rptd_Cnt_Yr_1 = Rptd_Cnt_Yr_1.y) |>
  select (!Rptd_Cnt_Yr_1.x) |>
  
  left_join(Cap_Var_DF, by = join_by(Dev_Yr)) |>
  left_join(Cap_Var_Sqrd_DF, by = join_by(Dev_Yr) )|>
  left_join(Spline_Var_DF, by = join_by(Dev_Yr) )|>
  left_join(Spline_Var_Sqrd_DF, by = join_by(Dev_Yr)) |>
  left_join(Spline_Var_Ln_DF, by = join_by(Dev_Yr)) |>
  left_join(Cap_Var_Ln_DF, by = join_by(Dev_Yr)) |>
  left_join(Factor_Var_DF, by = join_by(Dev_Yr)) |>
  left_join(Case_Inflation_Infl_Index, by = join_by(Cal_Yr)) |>
  mutate( Cal_Yr = Acc_Yr + Dev_Yr -1,
    Paid_Incr_Cnt_Freq = Paid_Cnt_Incr/Rptd_Cnt_Yr_1,
         Mean_Payment = Incr_Paid / Paid_Cnt_Incr,
          Infl_Index_Pct = Infl_Index -1,
         Ln_Mean_Payment = log(Mean_Payment),
         Incr_PP = Incr_Paid/ Rptd_Cnt_Yr_1,
         Ln_Incr_PP = log(Incr_PP),
         Incr_PP_Defl = Incr_PP/ Accum_Infl_Index_Mid,
         Ln_Incr_PP_Defl = log(Incr_PP_Defl),
         Mean_Payment_Defl = Mean_Payment/ Accum_Infl_Index_Mid,
         Ln_Mean_Payment_Defl = log(Mean_Payment_Defl),
         Cal_Yr_Time = Cal_Yr - min_Cal_Yr +1,
         Z_Count= if_else(Paid_Cnt_Incr ==0,1,0),
    Disp_Rate = round(if_else( Acc_Yr == lag(Acc_Yr) & is.na(lag(Acc_Yr)) == FALSE  ,
                               (Incr_Clsd_W_Pay_Cnt + Incr_Clsd_W_O_Pay_Cnt) /
                                 (Cum_Rptd_Cnt - lag(Cum_Rptd_Cnt)+ lag(Open_Cnt)),
                               (Incr_Clsd_W_Pay_Cnt + Incr_Clsd_W_O_Pay_Cnt) /
                                 Cum_Rptd_Cnt),3) ) |>
  filter(Cal_Yr >= 2026)



# subset training data sets

Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Train <- Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Complete |>
                      filter(Cal_Yr < 2026 ) 

# using "NZ" in the title was an internal naming device to indicate only
# non-zero payment observations would be included. 

Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Train_NZ <- Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Complete |>
  filter(Cal_Yr < 2026 & Z_Count != 1) 

Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Train_zero_count <- Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Train %>%
  group_by(Dev_Yr) %>%
  mutate(Prob_Zero =mean(Z_Count) )%>%
  select(Dev_Yr, Prob_Zero) %>%
  unique()

# the variance and shape components in the file below were not used
# since those only measured the between mean accident year group effects

Case_Inflation_Dev_Yr_mu_sd_train <- Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Train_NZ  %>%
  group_by(Dev_Yr) %>%
  mutate(Ln_Mean_Payment_mu =mean(Ln_Mean_Payment),
```

# Comments on EDA Graphs

The cumulative graphs indicate that:
•	Increases in reported claims after six years of development decline rapidly and reported claim counts after ten years of development are rare.
•	Open claim count peaks at about four years of development.
•	The rate of increase in paid claim count activity starts to decline at about six years of development and begins to taper off rapidly at about 10 years of development. 
•	Inflation (as measured in a general index) varies from year to year and ranges from 1.5% to 6%. 


A summary of what the incremental graphs indicate about the modeling problem includes: 
•	Incremental claim payments rise sharply from development year 1 to 4 and then start to decline.
•	Normalizing the incremental payments makes it easier to pick up the general pattern.
•	The normalized incremental pure premium exhibits a rough parabolic shape, although the first few development periods may not be fit well by a smooth curve. The curve peaks at four years of development and then starts to decline. 
•	The QQ plot indicates that the lognormal distribution could be a good candidate for modeling the incremental, deflated pure premium.
•	The average payments per claim by development year after removing the effect of the known inflation index tend to show an upward drift over the calendar years  indicating that some annual loss cost trend in addition to the inflation index is present. 
•	There is no indication that it’s necessary to use a mixture model to account for observations with zero claim payments at either the beginning or end of the accident year development time period. 
•	Sigma for the lognormal distribution follows a pattern that is different from mu. It drops after the first year, stays relatively low for a few development years then starts to increase as the accident year ages. 
•	If one chooses to use the Gamma distribution to model the incremental, deflated pure premium, it increases after the first development period  somewhat parabolic downward shape after 5 years of development which may be amenable to modeling as an alternative to the lognormal distribution. 


# Comments on Model 1  No Prior

The model below is designed to:  

- Let one see the reasonability of selected prior distribution parameters as starting points.  
- Model mu in two segments with the first four development period as categorical variables and the remaining development years as a declining parabolic curve.    
- Model sigma to reflect the it declines over the first development yearthen starts to increase  

Observations:  

- Given the wide range in the accident year intercepts since there is no data, the
predictions are not useful.  

- The no data modeled results for mu and sigma can give one a sense of plausible starting points.   

```{r}

# note that the standard deviations are very small to keep the results
# from blowing up given that there is no data to give information.




Case_Inflation_Prior_1_no_data <- c(prior(normal(-.05,.001),class=b, coef= Spline_Dev_Yr_4),
                            prior(normal(-.01,.001),class=b, coef= Spline_Dev_Yr_Sqrd_4),
                            prior(normal(1.5,.0025),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_42),
                            prior(normal(2,.0025),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_43),
                            prior(normal(2.5,.0025),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_44),
                            prior(normal(6.5,.005),class=b ,coef =Intercept),
                            prior(normal(.02,.005),class=b, coef=Cal_Yr_Time),
                            prior(normal(-1 ,.005),class=b ,coef =Intercept,dpar=sigma),
                            prior(normal(-.5,.001),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_42,dpar=sigma),
                            prior(normal(-.75,.001),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_43,dpar=sigma),
                            prior(normal(-.8,.001),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_44,dpar =sigma),
                            prior(normal(.02 ,.0005),class=b, coef= Spline_Dev_Yr_4, dpar=sigma),
                            prior(student_t(2,.02,.0005),class=b, coef=Spline_Dev_Yr_8,dpar=sigma))

# note the use of the "sample_prior = "only" " command to avoid using the data

Case_Inflation_Model_1_prior_only <- brm(bf(Incr_PP_Defl ~ 0 + Intercept + 
                                   Factor_Dev_Yr_4 + 
                                   Spline_Dev_Yr_4  +
                                   Spline_Dev_Yr_Sqrd_4 +
                                   Cal_Yr_Time +
                                   (1||Acc_Yr),
                                 sigma ~   0 + Intercept +
                                   Factor_Dev_Yr_4 + Spline_Dev_Yr_4 +
                                   Spline_Dev_Yr_8
                                ),
                                iter= 2000,
                                save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
                                prior= Case_Inflation_Prior_1_no_data,
                                sample_prior = "only",
                                seed= 8603529,
                                data = Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Train_NZ, 
                                family = lognormal()
                                )


model_summary_information( Case_Inflation_Model_1_prior_only)


model_fit_lognormal_no_data(Case_Inflation_Model_1_prior_only, 
                    Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Train_NZ
                    )



```

# Comments on Model 2  
/  
Model design:  

- The revisions to Model 1 were to put in an alternative model for sigma with
a better starting point for the intercept and a change for development to 
avoid high results for sigma in the later  development periods.   

Observations:  

- The model did coverage and the number of effective observations was high enough that the beta  
estimates are reliable.  
- The residuals improved and the modeled results appear to track the observations 


#Run Model 2

# Model 3 Comments  

Model 3 is intended to do the following:  

-  Demonstrate how to use the smooth spline option for mu.  
-  Alter the formula for sigma to reduce variability late in development time.  
-  Illustrate how to view conditional smoothing results  
-  Illustrate use of control = command to adjust MCMC parameters as needed
-  Illustrate that one can view the Stan code created by brms


Observations:  

- The model seems to fit better  
-  One could try running the model without the control = command to see the
warnings that Stan will produce  
-  Need to run loo later to evaluate the three lognormal models  

```{r}


options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())

Case_Inflation_Prior_3 <- c(
          prior(normal(1.5,.25),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_42),
          prior(normal(2,.25),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_43),
          prior(normal(2.5,.25),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_44),
          prior(normal(6.5,.25),class=b ,coef =Intercept),
          prior(normal(.02,.005),class=b, coef=Cal_Yr_Time),
          prior(student_t(3,-.75,.1),class=b ,coef =Intercept,dpar=sigma),
          prior(student_t(3,-.5,.1),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_32,dpar=sigma),
          prior(student_t(3,-.75,.1),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_33,dpar=sigma),
          
          prior(student_t(3,.2 ,.05),class=b, coef= Spline_Dev_Yr_4, dpar=sigma)
         )

Case_Inflation_Model_3 <- brm(bf(Incr_PP_Defl ~ 0 + Intercept + 
                                   Factor_Dev_Yr_4 + 
                                   s(Dev_Yr) +
                                   Cal_Yr_Time +
                                   (1||Acc_Yr),
                                 sigma ~  0 + Intercept + 
                                   Factor_Dev_Yr_3 + Spline_Dev_Yr_4
                                ),
                              control=list( max_treedepth = 15,
                                            adapt_delta = .99),
                                iter= 2000,
                                save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
                                prior= Case_Inflation_Prior_3,
                                seed= 8603529,
                                data = Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Train_NZ, 
                                family = lognormal()
                                )


cat(stancode(Case_Inflation_Model_3))

model_summary_information( Case_Inflation_Model_3)



model_fit_lognormal(Case_Inflation_Model_3, 
                    Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Train_NZ,
                    Case_Inflation_Dev_Yr_mu_sd_train,
                    Case_Inflation_Dev_Yr_ran_grp_NZ_mu_sd_train)


conditional_smooth_dev_Yr <- plot(conditional_smooths(Case_Inflation_Model_3))

conditional_smooth_dev_Yr[[1]] +
  labs(
    title ="Smoothing Spline by Development Year",
    subtitle = "Case_Inflation_Model_3",
    x = "Development Year",
    y= "Smooth Spline",
    caption ="Data set: Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Train_NZ")



```

# compare the lognormal models using loo  

- For each model the WAIC, loo and method of moments loo is produced  
- There three tables at the end which show the WAIC, loo and method of moments loo
-  The method of moments loo is sometimes needed to correct for high K values
- The loo package will have documentation on how to interpret the warnings that come out  
- Model 3 is evaluated to be the best, but the differences are small in this case.

# Run model 4 routines  

This is Gamma model for the normalized, incremental pure premium.  

This model uses a parabolic curve for mu after four years of development.  

Note that "shape" replaces "sigma" for the non mean parameter.  





```{r}



options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())

Case_Inflation_Prior_4 <- c(prior(normal(-.05,.01),class=b, coef= Spline_Dev_Yr_4),
                            prior(normal(-.01,.01),class=b, coef= Spline_Dev_Yr_Sqrd_4),
                            prior(normal(1.5,.25),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_42),
                            prior(normal(2,.25),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_43),
                            prior(normal(2.5,.25),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_44),
                            prior(normal(6.5,.25),class=b ,coef =Intercept),
                            prior(normal(.02,.005),class=b, coef=Cal_Yr_Time),
                            prior(student_t(3,4,.1),class=b ,coef =Intercept,dpar=shape),
                            prior(student_t(3,.75,.1),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_32,dpar=shape),
                            prior(student_t(3,1.0,.1),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_33,dpar=shape),
                            prior(student_t(3,-.1 ,.05),class=b, coef= Spline_Dev_Yr_8, dpar=shape),
                            prior(student_t(3,-.2 ,.05),class=b, coef= Spline_Dev_Yr_4, dpar=shape)
                            )



Case_Inflation_Model_4 <-brm(bf(Incr_PP_Defl ~ 0 +Intercept +
                          Factor_Dev_Yr_4 + 
                          Spline_Dev_Yr_4 +
                          Spline_Dev_Yr_Sqrd_4 +
                          
                          Cal_Yr_Time + 
                          (1||Acc_Yr), 
                        shape ~ 0 + Intercept +
                          Spline_Dev_Yr_4 + Spline_Dev_Yr_8 +
                           Factor_Dev_Yr_3
                          ),
                          data = Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Train_NZ,
                          save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
                          iter=2000,
                          seed= 8603529,
                        control=list( max_treedepth = 15,
                                      adapt_delta = .99),
                          family=Gamma(link = "log"),
                          prior =Case_Inflation_Prior_4)

# Display summary results 

model_summary_information(Case_Inflation_Model_4)

# Compare actual to fitted observations

model_fit_gamma (Case_Inflation_Model_4, 
                 Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Train_NZ,
                 Case_Inflation_Dev_Yr_mu_sd_train,
                 Case_Inflation_Dev_Yr_ran_grp_NZ_mu_sd_train)





```
#  Try the Gamma distribution using a smoothing spline for mu

```{r}



Case_Inflation_Prior_5 <- c(
                            prior(normal(1.5,.25),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_42),
                            prior(normal(2,.25),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_43),
                            prior(normal(2.5,.25),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_44),
                            prior(normal(6.5,.25),class=b ,coef =Intercept),
                            prior(normal(.02,.005),class=b, coef=Cal_Yr_Time),
                            prior(student_t(3,4,.1),class=b ,coef =Intercept,dpar=shape),
                            prior(student_t(3,.75,.1),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_32,dpar=shape),
                            prior(student_t(3,1.0,.1),class=b, coef= Factor_Dev_Yr_33,dpar=shape),
                            prior(student_t(3,-.1 ,.05),class=b, coef= Spline_Dev_Yr_8, dpar=shape),
                            prior(student_t(3,-.2 ,.05),class=b, coef= Spline_Dev_Yr_4, dpar=shape)
                            )



Case_Inflation_Model_5 <-brm(bf(Incr_PP_Defl ~ 0 +Intercept +
                                  Factor_Dev_Yr_4 + 
                                  s(Dev_Yr) +
                                  
                                  Cal_Yr_Time + 
                                  (1||Acc_Yr), 
                                shape ~ 0 + Intercept +
                                  Spline_Dev_Yr_4 + Spline_Dev_Yr_8 +
                                   Factor_Dev_Yr_3
                                ),
                                data = Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Train_NZ,
                                save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
                                iter=2000,
                                seed= 8603529,
                                     control=list( max_treedepth = 15,
                                                   adapt_delta = .99),
                                family=Gamma(link = "log"),
                                prior =Case_Inflation_Prior_5)

# Display summary results

# Compare actual to fitted observations

model_fit_gamma (Case_Inflation_Model_5,

                 Case_Inflation_Dev_Yr_ran_grp_NZ_mu_sd_train)
```

# Compare the Models  

Compare Model_5 built with Gamma with the two best lognormal models.  

The comparison includes both the waic and loo results to give the reader exposure  
to the two common forecast comparison tools. It also shows the diagnostics  
generated along the way on the reliability of the forecasting comparison measures.  

The loo comparison tends to work better in terms of being more reliable for  
forecasting, but both WAIC and loo are shown to give a complete exposure to  
these comparison tools.  

In the end, the three models below don't differ appreciably in forecasting 
reliability.

# Calculate the predicted reserves using the results from three models and
# the forecasted inflation.  

The graphs present a dilemna in that the forecast reliability is not that different
between them, yet Model_2 would have a noticeably different reserve forecast.  

This brings up the issue of model risk which may, in practice, mean using an 
average of the model forecasts.  


```{r}


title_df <-compare_titles_3(Case_Inflation_Model_2,
                            Case_Inflation_Model_3,
                            Case_Inflation_Model_5,
                            Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Train_NZ)
  

Predicted_Inflation_Forecast_1 <-Generate_Predicted_Inflation_Forecast (8000,
                                                     Case_Inflation_Infl_Index,
                                                   8603529,
                                                    .03,
                                                    .01,
                                                    
                                                    2026,
                                                    2060) 


create_model_predicted_forecasts (Case_Inflation_Model_2,
                                  Case_Inflation_Model_3,
                                  Case_Inflation_Model_5,
                                  Case_Inflation_Acc_Yr_Dev_Yr_Future,
                                  Predicted_Inflation_Forecast_1,
                                  title_df)




```
